transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining today's pre-approval huddle. As you know, our middle-school mathematics assessment is scheduled for May 14, 2027, and I've circulated the draft administration plan for your review. Before I give my final approval, I'd like to hear from each of you on the plan as it currently stands -- digital testing on school tablets, all 26 students together in Room 201, one proctor, graphing calculators available throughout, and completed materials stored in the general records cabinet. Please share any concerns or recommendations you have.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue with the room and proctor setup in the draft plan. My finalized roster has 26 students, but the state administration manual limits a testing room to 14 students. I've already prepared Room 201 for 14 students and Room 202 for the remaining 12 students. Additionally, state testing supervision rules require one proctor assigned to each testing room, which means we need two proctors -- not one. I should also note that the updated room plan has not yet been entered into the district tracker.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue with the calculator policy in the draft plan. My review of the current state mathematics assessment manual shows that calculators may be used only on section 2 of the assessment, and they must be four-function calculators -- not graphing calculators. The draft plan currently calls for graphing calculators to be available throughout the entire assessment, which would violate state testing guidelines. I found this while checking the teacher materials this week but have not yet amended the draft plan.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical issue with the device setup in the draft plan. My device test found that the 26 assigned tablets cannot run the required secure testing application, and we cannot obtain compatible devices before May 14. I contacted the assessment vendor, who confirmed that paper booklets are authorized for this administration. However, this result has not yet been added to the draft plan, so the plan still calls for digital testing on school tablets, which is not feasible given the compatibility issue.

My security review of the state testing agreement, completed this week, requires that completed assessment materials be sealed in tamper-evident envelopes and stored in a locked cabinet for exactly 30 calendar days. The draft plan currently calls for completed materials to be stored in the general records cabinet, which does not meet these security requirements.
